study_identification_part.si4_title: A normative modelling approach reveals age-atypical cortical thickness in a subgroup of males with autism spectrum disorder

answer: ABIDE I/II structural MRI cortical thickness dataset (male-focused subset: TD n≈624, ASD n≈699 after QC/normative selection)
dc1_datasets_using_in_this_study.detail: Multi-site ABIDE cohorts providing cortical thickness data; normative modelling performed on typically developing males with ASD males evaluated for age-related deviations
dc1_datasets_using_in_this_study.supporting_text: "Across a large sample ( n = 870 per group) and wide age range (5-40 years), we applied normative modelling ... answer.ABIDE TD males: train age-related normative (LOESS) models for cortical thickness
answer.ABIDE ASD males: apply normative models to compute w-scores, identify age-atypical cortical thickness and prevalence

dc2_purpose_of_each_dataset.detail: TD male subset defines age-specific means/SDs via LOESS regression; ASD males receive w-scores relative to TD norms to quantify deviations and subgroup prevalence
dc2_purpose_of_each_dataset.supporting_text: "Normative modelling of age-related CT effects was done utilizing male-only data from the typically developing group ... These statistical norms were then used to compute a w-score ... for every individual with autism"
